why: The student claims public static void main() without String[] args works because the program uses no arguments. This is the documented MainWithoutStringArgs wrong rule: such a header compiles, but java Hello cannot launch the class because there is no proper main entry point.

concepts.quote: main() without String[] args is fine because the program uses no arguments.
concepts.why: This matches the MainWithoutStringArgs error: the String[] args parameter is required for the entry point whether or not the program reads any arguments.
The answer mentions that no arguments are used, but it makes no claim about how command-line arguments work.
The answer says nothing explicit about running the program.
